Young Richard Hayman held up well under pressure but the crash was going to come and an unfit Jim Estall bore the brunt of it having volunteered to step out of the car and into number three slot while the rest of the team was sorted out.
Richard Hayman, a complete novice to racing, took over next and ran a time which could well see his name among the 24 entries for the National 12-Stage.
Richard Hayman was not looking too comfortable but those "toughies" Rob McHarg, Will Cockerell and Joachim Wolf were running strongly with Norwegian Knut Hegvold also making an impression.

Twenty-one year-old Richard Hayman made another advance up the order to place 16th and a betting man might well be advised to have a few bob on Rick's chances of spending next year's series in the top ten.

Cap'n Rog. enjoyed the first event of his stag weekend, going some 15 seconds faster than anticipated to bring the Bels home to 3rd on stage 1, while Rick Hayman was only 10 seconds behind for the 'B's.
Not far behind came Richard Hayman running his best ever race and at only a few days past his 21st birthday another great prospect. Will Cockerell raised his game to a new level.

Twelve months earlier 21 year-old Rick Hayman had barely started running and now, as reserve, he grabbed his chance to go into the team. An 8:47 track 3,000 metres during the week had given him confidence and he kept the forward momentum going by overtaking the blue and white vested Bedford man to move us into 9th.

The race covers 47 miles, climbing 6,300 feet and there are five stages with runners from each team racing in pairs. Second team were Horwich RMI whose team included Paul Freary and Rick Hayman, running together.
